title: Interleave two increments without losing one
description: Start with counter = 0. Workers A and B each intend to add exactly one. Change the attempted schedule and synchronization rule, then inspect every operation.

schedules.label: A completes before B reads
schedules.detail: This schedule produces the expected value even without protection.

schedules.label: Both read 0; A writes first
schedules.detail: B keeps a stale local value while A commits.

steps.detail: B calculates the same local value 1
B writes its stale local value 1

schedules.label: Both read 0; B writes first
schedules.detail: A keeps a stale local value while B commits.

steps.detail: A calculates from its earlier read: local value 1
A writes its stale local value 1

strategies.label: No synchronization
strategies.detail: Run the selected read, compute, and write sequence as-is.
strategies.guarantee: There is no ordering edge between the workers' read-modify-write operations. A correct result in one schedule is accidental, not guaranteed.

strategies.label: Mutex around read-modify-write
strategies.detail: Only one worker can execute the whole counter transition at a time.
strategies.guarantee: The mutex serializes both critical sections. The later worker reads the value committed by the earlier worker before calculating its increment.

strategies.label: Atomic compare-and-swap loop
strategies.detail: A stale expected value fails instead of overwriting newer state.
strategies.guarantee: Each successful compare-and-swap commits one indivisible counter transition. A worker that observed stale state must load again and retry.

strategies.label: Single owner with commands
strategies.detail: Workers send increment commands; only the owner mutates the counter.
strategies.guarantee: Counter writes are serial because one task owns the state. Correctness now also depends on queue ordering, bounded capacity, and command delivery semantics.
